target.title: fix(openai): bound Codex OAuth token response body reads with readResponseWithLimit
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The OpenAI Codex OAuth token endpoint `postTokenForm` helper used unbounded `response.arrayBuffer()` for both token exchange and refresh operations. An oversized response from `https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token` could force the gateway process to buffer until OOM.

**Solution**: Replace `response.arrayBuffer()` with `readResponseWithLimit` using a 1 MiB `OAUTH_TOKEN_RESPONSE_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES` cap, matching the same pattern used by alix-007 across 30+ providers.

**What changed**:
- `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.ts` — added `readResponseWithLimit` import, bounded constant, replaced unbounded `response.arrayBuffer()` in `postTokenForm()`
- `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.test.ts` — added real `node:http` loopback server tests (happy path under-cap + over-cap rejection)

**What did NOT change**: No protocol logic, error handling paths, or caller behavior modified. Error-path `response.text()` calls in `exchangeAuthorizationCode` and `refreshAccessToken` read already-bounded in-memory buffers (the body is capped by `postTokenForm`).

## What Problem This Solves

Users who configure OpenAI Codex OAuth authentication have no protection against oversized token endpoint responses. The `postTokenForm` helper reads the full response body without any byte cap, so an unexpectedly large response from the token endpoint could exhaust gateway memory during OAuth token exchange or refresh. This is the same class of issue fixed by alix-007 across 30+ other providers (Discord, Matrix, Google, xAI, etc.).

## Why This Change Was Made

`postTokenForm` is the single network read path for both `exchangeAuthorizationCode` and `refreshAccessToken`. Replacing `response.arrayBuffer()` with `readResponseWithLimit` at this single entry point protects both callers without code duplication. The 1 MiB cap is orders of magnitude larger than any legitimate token JSON payload (~1-2 KB), so it safely rejects oversized payloads with a clear error.

The proof uses real `node:http` loopback servers on `127.0.0.1` with random ports. The tests route real `exchangeAuthorizationCode` calls through the production `postTokenForm` path to the loopback server.

## User Impact

Operators using OpenAI Codex OAuth authentication no longer risk gateway OOM from an oversized token endpoint response. Normal OAuth token payloads under the 1 MiB cap continue to work without any change in behavior.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: OpenAI Codex OAuth token responses are now read with `readResponseWithLimit` instead of unbounded `response.arrayBuffer()`.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.13.1

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```terminal
cd openclaw/.worktrees/unbounded-oauth
pnpm test extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.test.ts
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 12 tests pass (10 existing + 2 new loopback proof tests).

**After-fix evidence**:
```terminal_output
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  12 passed (12)
   Start at  17:26:24
   Duration  3.08s (transform 2.79s, setup 1.49s, import 529ms, tests 569ms, environment 0ms)
```

Loopback proof:
- Happy path: `exchangeAuthorizationCode` returns `type: "success"` with correct token values from a real HTTP server
- Over-cap: `exchangeAuthorizationCode` returns `type: "failed"` with "too large" in error message (2 MiB over 1 MiB limit)

**What was not tested**: Full gateway E2E OAuth login flow (requires live OpenAI auth endpoint); the change is purely a network read boundary in the token request helper with no protocol logic change.

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Low risk — additive boundary protection, no existing behavior modified
- [x] No runtime logic changes — only network read path in a single helper function
- [x] Negative test verifies oversized responses are rejected with "too large" error
- [x] Existing mock-based tests unaffected (all pass)
- [x] Pattern matches alix-007's established fix across 30+ providers
